metaTitle: BMW Engine Inspection & Assessment | BMW Garage
metaDescription: Full BMW engine inspection & assessment at BMW Garage. We strip, measure & assess your BMW engine to determine what work is required. Book today.
lede: We strip, inspect and measure your BMW engine to determine exactly what work is required — then quote you the work that actually needs doing.

sections.heading: What a BMW Engine Inspection & Assessment Involves

blocks.html: An engine inspection and assessment is the process we follow to determine the condition of your BMW engine and what work is required. This is **not** a diagnostic process focused on failure symptoms — it is the physical inspection that happens after a problem has been identified.

We assess the engine thoroughly, from initial visual checks through to full strip-down and component measurement. The outcome is a detailed scope of work and a quotation based on what your engine actually needs.

Because BMW engines vary significantly across models and generations, our assessment process is adapted to each specific engine type — whether it's a 4-cylinder diesel with a rear-mounted timing chain or a high-performance S58 from an M3.

paras: Includes strip-down, component inspection and quotation. Excludes engine removal/refit — quoted separately where required.

sections.heading: Which BMW Models & Engines We Assess

blocks.html: Our inspection and assessment process covers the full BMW range — from 1 Series to X7, including M-cars. We assess the engine in its specific vehicle application, not just by engine code alone.
Key variants we regularly assess include:

items: [M5 Competition (S63)](/bmw-m5-competition-engines) — hot-vee turbo & valve seal assessment

blocks.html: We also assess [M2](/bmw-m2-engines), [M6](/bmw-m6-engines), [8 Series](/bmw-8-series-engines) and all [X3 M](/bmw-x3-m-engines) / [X4 M](/bmw-x4-m-engines) models.

steps.title: Initial Visual Inspection
steps.body: The engine bay is inspected for leaks, damaged components, missing parts or physical damage.

steps.title: Fluid Assessment
steps.body: Oil, coolant and other fluids are checked for contamination, levels and condition.

steps.title: Component Inspection
steps.body: Belts, hoses, wiring and sensors are examined for condition and wear.

steps.title: Engine Removal (if required)
steps.body: For a full assessment, the engine is removed from the vehicle and mounted on a stand.

steps.title: Strip-Down
steps.body: The engine is systematically disassembled — cylinder head removed, sump dropped, internals exposed.

steps.title: Component-by-Component Inspection
steps.body: Each component is inspected for wear and condition. Critical measurements are taken: bore wear, crankshaft journal condition, bearing wear, valve guide wear.

steps.title: Machinability Assessment
steps.body: Components are assessed to determine whether they can be machined back to specification or must be replaced.

steps.title: Quotation
steps.body: A detailed scope of work and quotation is prepared based on the inspection findings.

sections.heading: How a BMW Engine Assessment Works

steps.body: You contact us — by phone, email or the quote form — with your BMW's registration or engine details.
We agree the scope — whether an initial bay inspection or a full engine-out strip-down assessment.
Your BMW arrives at our workshop (or we recover it — [nationwide recovery available](/bmw-engine-recovery)).
We carry out the inspection and strip-down per the agreed scope.
We provide a detailed quotation — with clear costs and a firm recommendation.
You decide whether to proceed with the work (rebuild, replacement or repair).

items.q: How long does a BMW engine inspection take?
items.a: An initial bay inspection takes 1–2 hours. A full engine-out strip-down assessment typically takes 1–2 days, depending on engine complexity and access.

items.q: How much does an engine assessment cost?
items.a: Our standard inspection and assessment starts from £250 + VAT. This includes strip-down, component inspection and a detailed quotation. Engine removal and refit are quoted separately where required.

items.q: Do you assess M-car engines (S55, S58, S63)?
items.a: Yes. We regularly assess S55 (M2 Competition / M3 / M4), S58 (X3 M / X4 M / G80 M3) and S63 (M5 / M6 / M8) engines. These require specific procedures, which we have in-house.

items.q: What if you find more damage during the assessment?
items.a: We quote the work based on what we find. If additional issues are discovered during strip-down, we pause, call you with the updated findings, and agree a revised scope before proceeding.

items.q: Do you assess BMW diesel engines with timing chain issues?
items.a: Yes. We assess N47, B47 and N57 diesel engines — including the rear-mounted timing chain systems found in 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, X1, X3 and X5 models.
